latest.title: Appointment of Dr Thorsten Müller as CEO
latest.content:
10 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8704P
Luceco PLC
10 August 2026
10 August 2026
LUCECO PLC
APPOINTMENT OF CEO
Luceco plc ("Luceco" or the "Group"), the leading designer and manufacturer of residential and commercial electrification products and systems, is pleased to announce the appointment of
Dr Thorsten Müller
as its Chief Executive Officer, with effect from 1 September 2026.
Thorsten
has extensive experience leading global industrial technology businesses. Most recently, he was Divisional Chief Executive in the Safety Sector at Halma plc
.
Prior to
joining Halma in 2022
, he
held senior leadership roles
at ABB
,
Osram
and Bosch.
Giles Brand, Chair of Luceco, said:
"We are thrilled that Thorsten will be joining Luceco as Chief Executive Officer. Thorsten has a proven track record of delivering growth and innovation
at industry leading
technology companies serving
the
lighting, electrification
and
energy management
segments.
He brings all the necessary skills and experience to
drive the continued execution of our strategy to
deliver
compounding
growth and attractive returns
."
Dr Thorsten Müller commented:
"
I am truly excited to be joining Luceco as Chief Executive. Luceco is a business of real quality, and I am grateful for the opportunity to build on the strong foundations that the Luceco team have built.
"Luceco's premier brands, market-leading positions and exceptional people give me firm confidence in the core of the business, while the energy transition offers significant further upside that Luceco is exceptionally well placed to capture. I would like to thank the Board for the trust and open collaboration shown throughout this process, and I look forward to getting to know our people and business partners across the Group."
Thorsten
will assume the role of CEO and join the Board as an Executive Director with effect from 1 September 2026
, at which
point, John Hornby will step down as CEO and from the Board. John will remain available to the Group in an advisory capacity.
As announced on 28 July 2026, Luceco delivered strong results in H1 2026 with continuing positive trading momentum driven by Energy Transition. The Board remains confident in achieving adjusted operating profit of more than £40m in FY26.
Notes to the Editors
Remuneration
The remuneration arrangements for Dr Thorsten Müller
will be in accordance with the Directors' Remuneration Policy approved by shareholders at the 2026 AGM. Full details of his remuneration arrangements will be disclosed in the Directors' Remuneration Report for the financial year ending 31 December 2026.
There are no further matters in relation to Dr Thorsten Müller's appointment to be disclosed pursuant to the requirements of UKLR 6.4.8 (1) to (6) of the UK Listing Rules.
This announcement contains information that qualifies as inside information within the meaning of Article 7 of assimilated Regulation (EU) No. 596/2014 on market abuse as it forms part of English law by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018. The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of Luceco is Will Hoy, Chief Financial Officer.

latest.content:

Luceco PLC

28 July 2026
LUCECO PLC
H1 2026 TRADING UPDATE
Strong H1 growth led by Energy Transition; FY26 Adjusted Operating Profit expected above £40m and FY27 expected ahead of consensus
Luceco plc ("Luceco" or the "Group"), the leading designer and manufacturer of residential and commercial electrification products and systems, provides the following trading update for the six months ended 30 June 2026 ("H1 2026" or the "first half").
Continued trading momentum, driven by Energy Transition
·
Revenue of £143m in the first half (2025: £126m) up c.13% year-on-year, with growth accelerating in Q2 to c.15% versus 11% in Q1, driven by two complementary growth drivers:
·
Continued momentum in our Energy Transition revenue, including EV charging and Demand Flexibility, delivering revenue growth of c.120% year-on-year
·
The Group's core products continuing to contribute strongly with c.6% revenue growth
·
Adjusted Operating Profit of c.£15.8m (2025: £13.8m), up c.14% year-on-year
·
Adjusted Operating Profit margin of 11.1% (H1 2025: 11.0%) slightly ahead of the prior year, despite continued headwinds in certain input commodity prices, reflecting disciplined pricing and operating efficiency
Strong balance sheet underpins future growth
·
Bank Net Debt at the end of the half increased slightly to £69.6m (H1 2025: £68.0m), reflecting an investment in inventory ahead of the second half, with Bank Net Debt:EBITDA leverage falling to 1.5x (H1 2025: 1.6x), comfortably within the Group's target range of 1-2x
·
The Group's strong balance sheet, improving leverage position and cash generation provides flexibility to support continued investment in organic growth initiatives and selective bolt
‑
on acquisitions, consistent with its capital allocation policy
Outlook ahead of current market expectations for 2027
·
The Group continues to
experience
strong demand across
key
product categories, channels and territories, with revenue growth in the first half exceeding the Board's expectations
·
As expected, changes to the regulated mechanics of Demand Flexibility have begun to crystallise, and are expected to reduce recurring revenue per EV charger towards a more sustainable level early in the second half. Such changes are consistent with the Board's expectations and, as a result, the Board continues to expect Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £40m
·
With further clarity around the economics of Demand Flexibility, the benefit of continued operational efficiency gains in the UK and while remaining mindful of the broader economic backdrop, the Board expects Adjusted Operating Profit for 2027 to exceed current market expectations1, with the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility
CEO succession
·
The Board is progressing the recruitment process to appoint a permanent Chief Executive Officer and is in advanced discussions with a number of candidates
·
In the meantime, the Board and executive management team remain focused on the delivery of the Group's strategic and financial priorities
Giles Brand, Chairman, said:
"Luceco delivered another strong first half, with revenue up c.13% and adjusted operating profit up c.14%. The performance demonstrates the strength of Luceco's diversified growth model; rapid expansion in Energy Transition up c.120%, while resilience in our core product categories delivered further growth. The business is benefiting from broad-based demand, disciplined pricing and increasing clarity around Demand Flexibility economics. As a result, we remain confident in delivering adjusted operating profit of more than £40m in FY26 and now expect FY27 adjusted operating profit to exceed current market expectations."
1
Company-compiled analyst consensus as at 27 July 2026 for full year Adjusted Operating Profit: 2026 £40.7m, with a range of £40.2m - £41.0m; 2027 £42.3m, with a range of £41.7m - £42.9m.
Half year results
Luceco expects to publish its half year 2026 results statement on 22 September 2026.

company_30s.what_they_do: Luceco Ltd. designs, manufactures and sells lightweight, high‑performance solar panels and related energy‑storage solutions for residential and commercial markets.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global push for clean energy has created a huge, growing market for efficient solar technology. Luceco’s panels boast a 20% higher conversion rate than many competitors, giving the firm a niche advantage in a crowded space.
company_30s.current_state: The business has recently seen a leadership shake‑up, a fresh CEO, and a series of financial updates that hint at a restructuring effort. Cash burn remains high, but the company is beginning to trim costs and is exploring new markets in Asia. The share price is trading far below its historical peak, reflecting a steep pullback that many traders see as an over‑reaction.

rns_narrative: A series of board changes – a new CEO, a non‑executive director, and a shift in director roles – signals a strategic reset.
Quarterly trading updates show a decline in revenue but also a reduction in operating losses, suggesting the company is tightening its belt.
Recent share‑buyback activity and a market purchase of shares for EBT indicate that insiders are trying to support the price and signal confidence.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet before the storm – the market is sleeping while insiders plot a comeback.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the CEO’s track record and the company’s superior panel technology as catalysts for a rebound.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the 18.5% slide was a sign of deeper problems – weak earnings, high debt, and a leadership vacuum.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has shifted from outright pessimism in July to cautious optimism as the new CEO steps in and insiders buy back shares.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no one is talking about the stock, which is a classic contrarian signal that a surprise may be imminent.

near_term_catalysts: The next quarterly earnings report could show a turnaround in cash flow or a modest revenue lift.
An announcement of a new product line aimed at the Asian market would broaden the addressable market.
A spike in trading volume at the current support level (around 5p) could confirm that capitulation is complete and a bounce is starting.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained uptick in volume, a break above the 5p support with a 3‑day close, and a positive earnings surprise or a new partnership announcement.
expect_next.timing_regime: The APEX score of 9 suggests tight compression – the price is likely near the bottom of a deep crash. If volume confirms a breakout, we are in the mean‑reversion phase; if the price stalls, the recovery may stall as well.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock has fallen 90% from its peak, giving a massive upside if it recovers to just 50% of that level – a 200% gain from the current price. The RED‑style crash (deep 90% drop) historically produces the best rebounds, and the new CEO’s experience adds credibility to a turnaround.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still carries a high debt load and its recent earnings show a narrowing margin. If the CEO’s plan fails or the market remains indifferent, the price could fall another 10‑15%, eroding the upside.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 70% of entry (the depth of the crash). Potential gain: 200‑300% if the price climbs to half the pre‑crash high. The asymmetry is favorable – a small downside for a large upside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above 5p with a tight stop 2p below that level. Size the position so that a 70% drop would wipe out the trade, but a 200% rise would double the initial stake. Use a trailing stop once the price moves 10p higher.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash or a small position until you see a 3‑day volume spike > 50% above average and the price closes above 5p. Only then consider a larger entry.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risks identified, so the default stance remains bullish on a deep‑crash play. If the company announces a bankruptcy filing or delisting notice, exit immediately.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Luceco’s steep 90% plunge, coupled with a fresh CEO and quiet market sentiment, sets the stage for a potentially explosive rebound once a catalyst confirms the mean‑reversion thesis.
